960	conversation he writes: so what is the central piece of advice? Let's look
961	through all the counsels for the central one, and this
962	was a general guideline
963	that he reminded each and every one to do hitbodedut every
964	single day
965	and to pour out his speech before HaShem, may He be blessed,
966	and to ask Him with mercy and supplications for the merit
967	to draw close to His service. Set aside time every day to talk to
968	our Father in Heaven. See what an easy counsel it is. We said: don't
969	be clever, don't be sharp, you don't need to be
970	rich, you don't need to be a poet or a writer, you don't
971	need now to deliver some stirring speech with
972	tears, full of wise or deep words, nothing at all.
973	Something simple, simple, from the heart, sincere, even dry,
974	without feelings, without anything. Just speak.
975	And after he said all this, he says:
976	everything I am commanded to do
977	is very heavy to do. How strange!
978	You tell me: I have an easy rectification for you, the easiest
979	in the world. No tzaddik gave such an easy rectification to people
980	like these, may HaShem have mercy, who went through what they went through.
981	Why, why do you tell me it is so heavy?
982	Because of this it is heavy: because it weighs so much.
983	That is why it is heavy. It is not really heavy; it is heavy
984	because there are forces clothed around it: do everything
985	but not this. Do whatever you want, be great
986	in Torah, be a giver of charity, be wise, be
987	rich, be successful, raise children, do whatever
988	you want, just do not speak with the Holy One, blessed be He.
989	And if you try, we will ruin it for you. You will feel
990	that it does not come out well for you. For long periods
991	after I began to enter into this matter, I would come
992	to do hitbodedut and feel that I was burning,
993	I was hot, I was cold, I was itchy, annoyed, bored,
994	like, what do I have, what is in this? There is nothing in it.
995	Really hard feelings, and I would stop, and again
996	start, five minutes here, two minutes there, an hour
997	there, a year there.
998	Rabbi Nachman says: because it is so significant, it
999	will seem hard to you. In that same conversation Rabbi Natan says
1000	that his people, whoever believed him, did not count the difficulty,
1001	because he understood it was an imagined difficulty, not truly
1002	hard. I did not ask you to do hard labor. In the time of the Arizal, a man would come to the
1003	holy Ari, Rabbi Yitzchak Luria Ashkenazi, from whom all the Torah of Kabbalah
1004	came,
1005	and say to him: Listen, I committed such and such sins.
1006	The Arizal said: I know what you did, I see all your incarnations on you.
1007	Do you know what you need to do? You need
1008	to fast so and so many days, you need to mortify yourself, you need
1009	to abstain from this, you need to cleanse yourself
1010	with afflictions and mortifications of body and soul in order to be cleansed.
1011	Our Rebbe comes and says: I give you an easy task,
1012	and with it you will have a rectification
1013	for all the incarnations. But you have to believe me.
1014	You have to believe me. And there is also a test, and I even reveal
1015	the test to you. Do you know what the test is?
1016	That you will not feel anything, that you will not understand anything, that it will not
1017	go the way you want. Now, Rabbi Nachman is
1018	not the only one who spoke about this. The Chafetz Chaim.
1019	See what the Chafetz Chaim says.
1020	Likutei Amarim, chapter 10. The Chafetz Chaim writes as follows:
1021	all the troubles. He answers the question that we all
1022	ask all the time.
1023	Why all these troubles? How will we cancel
1024	the troubles from the Jewish people and from ourselves, so many troubles
1025	all around, and inside the home, and in the family, and illnesses and problems,
1026	and mental problems and anxieties, and money and shalom bayit,
1027	and children, and explosions and missiles, and what is going on, when
1028	will it end? The Chafetz Chaim says: I will give you a remedy
1029	for the situation of the whole generation and all your problems. I
1030	will give you the same remedy that Rabbi Nachman gives.
1031	See what he writes: all the troubles that come upon us,
1032	from which we have no rescue,
1033	are [because] we do not cry out and do not multiply
1034	prayer over them.
1035	Had we prayed and poured out our speech before the Holy One, blessed be He,
1036	surely our prayers and requests would not return
1037	empty. And a person should not content himself with praying the Amidah three
1038	times each day. I am not talking to you about the Amidah prayer,
1039	says the Chafetz Chaim, but how many times a day. He is
1040	stricter than our Rebbe: how many times a day one must
1041	pour out prayers
1042	and requests between himself and his Maker, when he is at home, from the depths
1043	of the heart, speak with the Holy One, blessed be He. And people who were
1044	close to the Chafetz Chaim would see that he did this
1045	every day: he would shut himself in a room, speak with HaShem
1046	in Yiddish, weeping to Him, telling Him his sorrow, the
1047	sorrow of the Jewish people. I can say, yes, but look how many troubles there still are. Who knows how many troubles
1048	were spared the Jewish people through the prayers of those
1049	who pray.
1050	
1051	I remember I had a friend in Emmanuel who wanted
1052	to do this. He wanted to organize
1053	that every night ten men would go out together
1054	to do hitbodedut in a field, to ask for mercy for the Jewish people. He gathered
1055	men who agreed, so that there would surely be ten.
1056	He gathered twenty, and he could not manage at all: these fell asleep, those
1057	did not get up. In the end about three remained. One did not come,
1058	one did not, did not go.
1059	Only one time it worked for him: he brought out ten men
1060	to pray, to ask for mercy for the Jewish people. The next
1061	morning a mass-casualty attack was prevented on the Ashkelon beach,
1062	where terrorists had arrived with all their equipment, up to
1063	the beach, and they caught them. I had no doubt that this was
1064	his work. Who knows from how many troubles we have already been
1065	saved thanks to this thing. So Rabbi Nachman says,
1066	and the Chafetz Chaim says, all the tzaddikim say, the Arizal
1067	says: our work is to speak with HaShem.
1068	See what our Rebbe writes further, Sichot HaRan. He answered
1069	and said: Is it conceivable that we leave HaShem, may He be blessed,
1070	to do and to think about decreeing decrees in the world?
1071	For we must call HaShem, may He be blessed, away from His affairs,
1072	in which He is engaged, in some decree and the like, Heaven forbid,
1073	to call Him away from there so that He will cast it aside and turn
1074	to us, to what we want to speak with Him, to ask Him
1075	to bring us closer to His service, may He be blessed. For when one
1076	of Israel wants to speak with HaShem, may He be blessed, to pour out his speech
1077	before Him, may He be blessed,
